A_target.statement: [[Definition:Merge Sort|Merge sort]] sorts $n$ keys using $\map \Theta {n \log n}$ comparisons in the worst case.

B_source.statement:
Let $\map T n = a \map T {n / b} + \map \Theta {n^d}$ with $a \ge 1$, $b > 1$, $d \ge 0$.
Then $\map T n = \map \Theta {n^d \log n}$ if $d = \log_b a$, $\map \Theta {n^d}$ if $d > \log_b a$, and $\map \Theta {n^{\log_b a} }$ if $d < \log_b a$.
This is the [[Master Theorem]].

object_map.reformulation: Read off the recurrence of merge sort and specialize the master theorem in its balanced case.

validity_conditions: Floors and ceilings in the recurrence do not change the asymptotic solution.
Merging two sorted lists of total length n uses at most n - 1 comparisons.
proof_plan: Merge sort splits the input into halves, sorts each recursively, and merges the results using at most $n - 1$ comparisons.
Here $a = 2$, $b = 2$ and $d = 1 = \log_2 2$, the balanced case of the source result.

Hence $\map T n = \map \Theta {n \log n}$, matching the [[Comparison Sort Lower Bound|comparison sorting lower bound]], so merge sort is asymptotically optimal.
{{qed}}
